Banyana Banyana

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Banyana Banyana players are making mark internationally, scoring contracts to play in professional leagues overseas.

Unique Selling Point:
The insert will profile Banyana Banyana players who have been signed by teams overseas, allowing them to play professionally in some of the world's biggest women's soccer leagues.

South Africa's national women's soccer team has enjoyed impressive successes over the years, albeit without the financial support enjoyed by their male counterparts.


Summary:
Although producing bright stars, women's soccer in the country is underdeveloped, doesn't have a professional league and often lacks the financial support necessary to grow the sport. Often female soccer players have to hold down second jobs and endure non-payment although they are the better performing national soccer team.

The insert will feature vignette style profiles of some of the players that have been signed overseas.

Thembi Kgatlana, joined Houston Dash in the States this year. (Interview Conducted)

Refiloe Jane (Interview Conducted)

Leandra Smeda

Linda Mathlalo

Banyana Banyana will represent South Africa in the AFCON tournament in Ghana, where if they make it to the top three, will qualify for the World Cup.

As a former Banyana Banyana player, who is aware of the difficulties women soccer players face in trying to make a career from the sport, Amanda Dlamini has made a career for herself as a television soccer commentator for Supersport. She will speak about the faults of the administrators of women's soccer by not giving the athletes adequate support and will also highlight the success of Banyana Banyana that have gone unnoticed.

The insert will include highlights of matches, where the above mentioned case studies have shined on the football field. We've already filmed Banyana Banyana training. The outstanding interviews will be done with a presenter, I imagine these to be more interactive, on the field and on the grandstands.

To acknowledge the great performance by the team, we'll do an interview with Coach Desiree Ellis on how she keeps her team motivated against the backdrop of a lack of support both financially and otherwise.

The country is set to have its first ever professional Women's League as of next year, Ria Ledwaba SAFA vice president will speak on why it's taken so long and what difference it'll make for developing women's soccer.

Script:


… (visuals of soccer fans at FNB stadium) Intro Link: Form the vuvuzela mad supporters, to its multi-millionnaire sport stars…South Africa loves soccer

Upsound ‘eBanyana Song’ – Aiport Arrival visuals
VO: A hero’s welcome for Banyana Banyana after they made history at the Africa cup of nations in Ghana.

Montage of goals and COSAFA Trophy ceremony/celebrations


Revert to Mac at Safa Wall of fame Link: Crowned COSAFA champions for two years in a row, Won South Africa’s team of the year for 2018, named CAF’s Women’s Team of the Year in 2017, produced the continent’s top goal scorer and steadily climbing up the rankings –

And now they have qualified to compete in the 2019 women’s Soccer World Cup – Banyana Banyana have become a formidable force on the field!

*Mamello playing vs Nigeria (from Superspost folder NGA V SA at 01:29 – 01:33) – then transition to player profile

Or

*Mamello corner kick (from Supersport folder SA vsMali 01:36 – 01:43)– transition to player profile





VO: Mamello Makhabane was first called up to Banyana Banyana at age 17. She’s represented the country at the Olympics twice and the chance to go to France next year is a dream come true for her.


Mamello atwork


Colleagues with TShirts
VO: She’s an aviation security officer at OR Tambo International and has been on special leave whilst representing the country in Ghana

VO: And when Banyana Banyan arrived back from the AFCON championships last week – her colleagues – joined the welcoming party to show their support







Highlights of Banyana vs Mali match
01:48 Mam: Eh I think now we’re more experienced than before and the team spirit was so high, we’re a unit from the technical task team to the palyers I think
we really really wanted this cause for most of us it was our last chance.
So obvious we had to do this for ourselves and the country and everyone who supports us




Visuals of Mac and Mamelo







Mamello at work
03:51 Mac: Even though you’ve played for such a long time you’ve been a part of the national team for many years as well but you still have to get a second job, why

04:02 Mam: I mean like you know South African women’s football we don’t earn a lot, like we don’t get anything so only when you play for the national team that’s when we get the little we can get eh so obviously we need to work to survive

Mamello at work






04:43 Mam: Ja it’s very difficult honestly cause it needs commitment, I mean I have to be committed to both of them, I have to be both at work and I have to train at the same time. I mean it is difficult but then like I said because eh I love soccer and I have to be committed to both cause I still need my job to survive

Link At SAFA House: From pay discrepancies to having to hold down a second job – Banyna Banyana players do not enjoy the same benefits and perks as their male counterparts, who make a living from the game. With all its accolades and achievements, the women’s national team is not reaping the rewards for its performance. SAFA has called on the corporate world to step up with sponsorships but in the meantime… how do we bridge the pay gap?

Cutaways of Mac and Ria




























VO: Ria Ledwaba is the South African Football Association’s Vice President – She says SAFA’s efforts to cash in on Banyana’s good record have previously been fruitless with SASOL being the only major committed sponsor


07:16 Ria:I think eh it’s a number of factors one the market out there has not really come on board in terms of supporting women’s football, you know you have a company like SASOL that has been supporting women’s football for the past ten years and SASOL themselves have gone out there to call on corporate to come on board and assist them but it hasn’t happened. Probably the success that we see now that south Africa is talking probably it will open up doors and for the next generation of girls to be able to achieve and to be able to be paid you know properly. Because you must remember SAFA is an organization that depends on the sponsors out there, so you go out there you get the sponsors for Bafana Bafana and that’s what they will be paid in terms of what we get. You go out there and you struggle to get companies to just support women’s football


02:35 Mac: You’ve got some players that have been with Banyana Banyana since they were seventeen years old. You look at someone like js*stutter you know they’ve been they’ve been there all the way. How do you lift the spirit of a Banyana player like that, that has given her youth and her entire adult life to Banyana Banyana but yet she still has to hold a second job to survive – what do you say to someone like that

03:11 Ria you know we are taking over school sport now we are looking at who else can be best to go to the schools and be able to to do better there. We are trying to talk to the CETAS to try an assist our girls to be able to empower them and the CETAS are coming on board to say we can take them to another level in terms of administration, in terms of coaching and we can place them with those schools to be able to do that for a number of years, from 1 to 3 years. So those are the things that we are trying as the association to be able to create an opportunity for girls to be able to participate, let’s see our girls playing a role in the structures we have


VO: An opportunity to learn technical and administrative skills – so they can be assistants to coaches or be trained for other jobs within SAFA structures. It can not go without saying, that the commitment to the team and the love for the game for Banyana Banyana players is a priceless sacrifice.

VO: Whilst adorning the national colours is a great honour for athletes - it also comes with monetary reward. For the women’s soccer team however the reward does not compare - to that of Bafana Bafana, the Boks or the Proteas.



Link Indoor Soccer field: Although under-resourced at grassroots level, women’s football is producing talented players and the world is beginning to take notice. More and more women are signing contracts with overseas teams, affording them the chance to play professionally and participate in highly competitive leagues. An opportunity that otherwise would not be available at home.
Video Of Thembi scoring Houston Dash goal and Dancing
From Thembi Kgatlana shows off her moves


Player profile

VO: Thembi Kgatlana was signed by U.S based Houston Dash in February this year.– joining Banyana Banyana Captain Janine Van Wyk and Midfielder Linda Mothlalo.






Second Video of Thembi Scoring
From Thembi kgatlana Makes it three video
13:01 Thembi: It has been an amazing feeling, coming from playing the sasol league which is a semi-pro league to going to Houston playing a professional sport, to being a professional athlete has been the most amazing thing I got to experience and something I’ve always wanted to be a part of.






Thembi stills + Thembi scoring against Nigeria (From Supersport Folder)
VO:Following her formidable performance at Houston Dash
Thembi’s contract has been extended for a new season.

The stellar striker was in top form at the AFCON tournament, finishing off as the top goal scorer and walking away with a player of the tournament trophy.


13:26 Thembi: It is, not a bit sad it is sad that you find other African countries that are not developed as South Africa, the likes of Kenya, having a professional league running, that likes of Nigeria and Cameroon, it’s really sad that South Africa doesn’t have a professional team with all the talent that we have, but it’s good to see that most of the female South African soccer players are getting contracts to play overseas. That means that there is something we’re doing right and despite not having a professional league in the country, it means that our players are motivated to work harder to get themselves professional contracts out of the country.


Player Profile + Refiloe stills




Canberra Highlights (From Refiloe Canberra) VO: Banyana Banyana Vice Captain Refiloe Jane signed to Australia side – Canberra United – along with fellow South African striker Rhoda Mulaudzi in August.

They were both discovered after an unknown persistent fan sent the Canberra coach youtube videos of the pair playing soccer.















Footage from Banyana Banyana Card2 – girls taking photographs outside SAFA House
03:46 Refiloe: Well we were in Cranberra the first two weeks of August and we had never done trails before, so when we were there and going through the paces, going through the training sessions, we didn’t know what to expect and looking at the time zones also, there was so much adjustments that we needed to do. But because we wanted this so bad, we had to pull through, whether you train in the rain, whether you train twice a day, whatever it takes you had to do it. And when they told us that we’ll be getting contracts, it was the best feeling ever.

VO: Refiloe has proved herself to be a valuable addition to Canberra – described by her Aussie coach as the backbone for the team.

04:49 Refiloe: Uhm I’d like to say that my journey starts now, it doesn’t mean that now I can settle and just be comfortable where I am, I need to be making sure that I am constantly working on my craft, I need to make sure that I improve my game, get a renewed contract when the season ends, if not get a better contract in some of the best leagues in the world you know. This isn’t just that you go to Australia and be happy that you play professional, it’s a continuous journey that you need to continue working on.

Amanda Stills








Highlights of Banyana Vs Equitorial Guinea (from Supersport)








Highlights of Banyana Vs Cameroon + Trophy Ceremony (From Kwese Sport folder)





Higlights of training at UJ Coach Desiree Ellis









Bus singing and celebration (from SASOL folder)
07:13 Amanda: it is I think a great step in the right direction

VO: Amanda Dlamini is a former Banyana Banyana Captain and soccer analyst – she believes players joining international teams is not only good for their individual careers but beneficial for the national team as well

07:15 Amanda: once our players are exposed to that sort of intensity in playing overseas then we know that we can also challenge in national duty and part of the reasons why we never really stepped up in the afriacn championships is because most of the Nigerian girls, Cameroonian girls, Ghanaian girls are playing overseas, they play in the French league, English and also in Chinana so they probably have the consistency and the temper of the game uhm the competitiveness of the game =, that kind of edge cause we have been – we’ve only been playing in the sasol structures where some of the teams don’t honour their fixtures which is a big big problem.


00:07 Mac: Amanda 2018 has been a great year for Banyana Banyana what would you say has made it such a good year for them

00:14 Amanda: Well I think we need to rewind and reflect on when coach Vera Pauw was still around, I think she did a great job in terms of laying a foundation for the girls and we competed yes in the African championships but we couldn’t qualify and there’s also a great coach eh in coach Deiree’s Calibre to also instill that continuation for the teams success I think uhm she’s picked quite a good crop of players that have been through the generations and I think also introduced a few faces from the sasol league and I think that fusion on it’s own is good to have a balance in the team and I think that has been the success for iBanayana that they’ve had the opportunity to build for a number of years to see the successs but of course it takes quite a lot of patience cause they’ve won the African championships and the championship title which I also think is goof for the country.

The road leading to their success and qualifying for the first time for France has been attributed to a lot of things that have happened within the structure




TUT vs UWC
+ Remarkable FC VO: For years now both players and supporters have been calling for a professional women’s league to be set up – much like the Premier Soccer League - it would mean regular competitive fixtures, broadcast games and salaries.

VO: However SAFA has opted to establish a national women’s league – saying for now - it’s a step in the right direction. The national league would see teams from provinces, the sasol league and varsity structures compete at higher level.

VO: But what about a professional women’s soccer league – SAFA says that mandate has been given to the PSL – but the PSL says it’s not involved in women’s football


11:28 RIA: Well eh we have a joint liaisons committee we always meet to debate issues of that nature I know in the last joint-committee meeting the issue of the professional league for women was raised that they should look into that but for now we are glad eh SAFA has created that platform for a national league


Singing in bus with we are going to france T-shirts


Airport Arivals/huggin officials/ signing autographs/ And Mamello going up escalators at aiport in Uniform
VO: Banyana Banyana’s qualifier for the women’s soccer world cup – has brought the lack of development and financial support in women’s football to the fore.



And the main message from South Africans on social media and other platforms – has been - Banyana deserve equal pay and in some instances more.

As strategies are being worked out to bring in more money – the administrators have challenged the nation to show it’s support at the stadiums.

We are trying to talk to the CETAS to try an assist our girls to be able to empower them and the CETAS are coming on board to say we can take them to another level in terms of administration, in terms of coaching and we can place them with those schools to be able to do that for a number of years, from 1 to 3 years. So those are the things that we are trying as the association to be able to create an opportunity for girls to be able to participate, let’s see our girls playing a role in the structures we have VO: An opportunity to learn technical and administrative skills – so they can be assistants to coaches or be trained for other jobs within SAFA structures. It can not go without saying, that the commitment to the team and the love for the game for Banyana Banyana players is a priceless sacrifice. VO: Whilst adorning the national colours is a great honour for athletes - it also comes with monetary reward. For the women’s soccer team however the reward does not compare - to that of Bafana Bafana, the Boks or the Proteas. Link Indoor Soccer field: Although under-resourced at grassroots level, women’s football is producing talented players and the world is beginning to take notice. More and more women are signing contracts with overseas teams, affording them the chance to play professionally and participate in highly competitive leagues. An opportunity that otherwise would not be available at home. Video Of Thembi scoring Houston Dash goal and Dancing From Thembi Kgatlana shows off her moves Player profile VO: Thembi Kgatlana was signed by U.S based Houston Dash in February this year.– joining Banyana Banyana Captain Janine Van Wyk and Midfielder Linda Mothlalo. Second Video of Thembi Scoring From Thembi kgatlana Makes it three video 13:01 Thembi: It has been an amazing feeling, coming from playing the sasol league which is a semi-pro league to going to Houston playing a professional sport, to being a professional athlete has been the most amazing thing I got to experience and something I’ve always wanted to be a part of. Thembi stills + Thembi scoring against Nigeria (From Supersport Folder) VO:Following her formidable performance at Houston Dash Thembi’s contract has been extended for a new season. The stellar striker was in top form at the AFCON tournament, finishing off as the top goal scorer and walking away with a player of the tournament trophy. 13:26 Thembi: It is, not a bit sad it is sad that you find other African countries that are not developed as South Africa, the likes of Kenya, having a professional league running, that likes of Nigeria and Cameroon, it’s really sad that South Africa doesn’t have a professional team with all the talent that we have, but it’s good to see that most of the female South African soccer players are getting contracts to play overseas. That means that there is something we’re doing right and despite not having a professional league in the country, it means that our players are motivated to work harder to get themselves professional contracts out of the country. Player Profile + Refiloe stills Canberra Highlights (From Refiloe Canberra) VO: Banyana Banyana Vice Captain Refiloe Jane signed to Australia side – Canberra United – along with fellow South African striker Rhoda Mulaudzi in August. They were both discovered after an unknown persistent fan sent the Canberra coach youtube videos of the pair playing soccer. Footage from Banyana Banyana Card2 – girls taking photographs outside SAFA House 03:46 Refiloe: Well we were in Cranberra the first two weeks of August and we had never done trails before, so when we were there and going through the paces, going through the training sessions, we didn’t know what to expect and looking at the time zones also, there was so much adjustments that we needed to do. But because we wanted this so bad, we had to pull through, whether you train in the rain, whether you train twice a day, whatever it takes you had to do it. And when they told us that we’ll be getting contracts, it was the best feeling ever. VO: Refiloe has proved herself to be a valuable addition to Canberra – described by her Aussie coach as the backbone for the team. 04:49 Refiloe: Uhm I’d like to say that my journey starts now, it doesn’t mean that now I can settle and just be comfortable where I am, I need to be making sure that I am constantly working on my craft, I need to make sure that I improve my game, get a renewed contract when the season ends, if not get a better contract in some of the best leagues in the world you know. This isn’t just that you go to Australia and be happy that you play professional, it’s a continuous journey that you need to continue working on. players joining international teams is not only good for their individual careers but beneficial for the national team as well 07:15 Amanda: once our players are exposed to that sort of intensity in playing overseas then we know that we can also challenge in national duty and part of the reasons why we never really stepped up in the afriacn championships is because most of the Nigerian girls, Cameroonian girls, Ghanaian girls are playing overseas, they play in the French league, English and also in Chinana so they probably have the consistency and the temper of the game uhm the competitiveness of the game =, that kind of edge cause we have been – we’ve only been playing in the sasol structures where some of the teams don’t honour their fixtures which is a big big problem. 00:07 Mac: Amanda 2018 has been a great year for Banyana Banyana what would you say has made it such a good year for them 00:14 Amanda: Well I think we need to rewind and reflect on when coach Vera Pauw was still around, I think she did a great job in terms of laying a foundation for the girls and we competed yes in the African championships but we couldn’t qualify and there’s also a great coach eh in coach Deiree’s Calibre to also instill that continuation for the teams success I think uhm she’s picked quite a good crop of players that have been through the generations and I think also introduced a few faces from the sasol league and I think that fusion on it’s own is good to have a balance in the team and I think that has been the success for iBanayana that they’ve had the opportunity to build for a number of years to see the successs but of course it takes quite a lot of patience cause they’ve won the African championships and the championship title which I also think is goof for the country. The road leading to their success and qualifying for the first time for France has been attributed to a lot of things that have happened within the structure TUT vs UWC + Remarkable FC VO: For years now both players and supporters have been calling for a professional women’s league to be set up – much like the Premier Soccer League - it would mean regular competitive fixtures, broadcast games and salaries. VO: However SAFA has opted to establish a national women’s league – saying for now - it’s a step in the right direction. The national league would see teams from provinces, the sasol league and varsity structures compete at higher level. VO: But what about a professional women’s soccer league – SAFA says that mandate has been given to the PSL – but the PSL says it’s not involved in women’s football 11:28 RIA: Well eh we have a joint liaisons committee we always meet to debate issues of that nature I know in the last joint-committee meeting the issue of the professional league for women was raised that they should look into that but for now we are glad eh SAFA has created that platform for a national league Singing in bus with we are going to france T-shirts Airport Arivals/huggin officials/ signing autographs/ And Mamello going up escalators at aiport in Uniform VO: Banyana Banyana’s qualifier for the women’s soccer world cup – has brought the lack of development and financial support in women’s football to the fore. And the main message from South Africans on social media and other platforms – has been - Banyana deserve equal pay and in some instances more. As strategies are being worked out to bring in more money – the administrators have challenged the nation to show it’s support at the stadiums.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Banyana Banyana players are making mark internationally, scoring contracts to play in professional leagues overseas.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The insert will profile Banyana Banyana players who have been signed by teams overseas, allowing them to play professionally in some of the world's biggest women's soccer leagues. South Africa's national women's soccer team has enjoyed impressive successes over the years, albeit without the financial support enjoyed by their male counterparts.
metadata.Summary: Although producing bright stars, women's soccer in the country is underdeveloped, doesn't have a professional league and often lacks the financial support necessary to grow the sport. Often female soccer players have to hold down second jobs and endure non-payment although they are the better performing national soccer team. The insert will feature vignette style profiles of some of the players that have been signed overseas. Thembi Kgatlana, joined Houston Dash in the States this year. (Interview Conducted) Refiloe Jane (Interview Conducted) Leandra Smeda Linda Mathlalo Banyana Banyana will represent South Africa in the AFCON tournament in Ghana, where if they make it to the top three, will qualify for the World Cup. As a former Banyana Banyana player, who is aware of the difficulties women soccer players face in trying to make a career from the sport, Amanda Dlamini has made a career for herself as a television soccer commentator for Supersport. She will speak about the faults of the administrators of women's soccer by not giving the athletes adequate support and will also highlight the success of Banyana Banyana that have gone unnoticed. The insert will include highlights of matches, where the above mentioned case studies have shined on the football field. We've already filmed Banyana Banyana training. The outstanding interviews will be done with a presenter, I imagine these to be more interactive, on the field and on the grandstands. To acknowledge the great performance by the team, we'll do an interview with Coach Desiree Ellis on how she keeps her team motivated against the backdrop of a lack of support both financially and otherwise. The country is set to have its first ever professional Women's League as of next year, Ria Ledwaba SAFA vice president will speak on why it's taken so long and what difference it'll make for developing women's soccer.
